Rarity.maps_to: Potion.rarity = 'rare' (potions.py:1236), read by shop.MerchantPotionEntry pricing and by potion_pools.POTION_POOL's rarity bucket (potion_pools.py:38-65)
Rarity.rationale: EXECUTED, not asserted: `py audit/tools/potion_probes.py sweep-attrs` extracts PotionRarity from every C# model and diffs it against the sim class attribute over all 51 units and reports 0 mismatches. Rarity is observable in the sim (it sets the shop price and the reward-roll bucket), so this is a behavioural verdict rather than a field copy.

Usage.maps_to: Potion.automatic = True (potions.py:1237); CombatState.use_potion refuses a manual use of it (combat.py:598-601)
Usage.rationale: PotionUsage.Automatic is the one Usage value the sim models, and it models the right one: the game disables the Use button for it and FairyInABottle.cs:21-26 says in so many words that OnUse 'should never be executed directly by UsePotionAction'. combat.py:600-601 returns False for `potion.automatic` before the slot is nulled, so a stray UsePotion action cannot spend it, and `py audit/tools/potion_probes.py sweep-attrs` confirms Automatic <-> automatic=True holds for this unit and no other. Note that Automatic is NOT AnyTime: nothing here needs the out-of-combat path that blood_potion's Usage gap is about.

TargetType.maps_to: no attribute -- `targeted` stays False, so CombatState.use_potion passes target=None (combat.py:608) and the potion applies to ctx.player (potions.py:1252-1256)
TargetType.rationale: TargetType.Self in a single-player run always resolves to the owner: PotionModel.EnqueueManualUse defaults `target` to `Owner.Creature` when it is a valid target (PotionModel.cs:240-243) and IsValidTarget's Self/AnyPlayer arms accept exactly that creature (PotionModel.cs:280-287). The multiplayer half -- AnyPlayer letting you throw the potion at an ally, and CanThrowAtAlly (PotionModel.cs:381-388) gating it on `RunState.Players.Count > 1` -- is out of scope by the shared contract and noted in maps_to rather than verdicted as a divergence.

CanBeGeneratedInCombat.maps_to: potion_pools.NOT_GENERATED_IN_COMBAT contains 'fairy_in_a_bottle' (potion_pools.py:75-77), consulted by generate_random_potion_in_combat (potion_pools.py:138-145) and by the legacy random_potion (potions.py:1269-1276)
CanBeGeneratedInCombat.rationale: EXECUTED: `grep -rn 'override bool CanBeGeneratedInCombat' src/` returns exactly three potions -- FairyInABottle.cs:19, FruitJuice.cs:20, RegenPotion.cs:22 -- and NOT_GENERATED_IN_COMBAT is exactly those three ids. The filter is applied where C# applies it (CreateRandomPotionInCombat, PotionFactory.cs:60-65) and NOT applied where C# does not (CreateRandomPotionOutOfCombat, :31-34), which is why Entropic Brew can still roll this potion in the parity path -- see potion/entropic_brew G2 for the legacy arm that gets that wrong.

ShouldDie.maps_to: FairyInABottle.should_die (potions.py:1242-1243), dispatched by hooks.should_die (hooks.py:588-594) from DamageCmd.deal step 7 (cmds.py:96-113)
ShouldDie.issue: The predicate itself is right and the DISPATCH PHASE is wrong. Body: `if (creature != Owner.Creature) return true; return false;` (FairyInABottle.cs:33-40) -- the fairy refuses only its owner's death and consents to everyone else's; potions.py:1243's `return creature.side != 'player'` is that same predicate in a single-player run, where the owner's creature is the only player-side creature. What diverges is WHICH PASS it runs in: Hook.cs:2229-2249 runs every ShouldDie listener first and only then every ShouldDieLate listener, so an early preventer like this one always gets first refusal over a Late one, and LizardTail is deliberately ShouldDieLate so other prevention triggers first. hooks.py:588-594 has ONE flat pass in listener-registration order. This is audit/records/seam/damage_pipeline.json guard N4, whose verdict was CORRECTED from waiver to gap by relic batch 8 precisely because its old rationale was 'FairyInABottle is a potion (out of scope)' and this potion is ported -- so this record is that waiver's counterexample and matches the corrected verdict per binding rule 3. LIVE, executed by that correction and by audit/records/relic/lizard_tail.json G4: with a Fairy in a Bottle held, the sim spends the TAIL (listener order ['LizardTail','FairyInABottle'], hp 41, fairy still in the belt) where the game always spends the fairy first. Both are ported and obtainable together.

AfterPreventingDeath.maps_to: FairyInABottle.after_preventing_death (potions.py:1245-1250), dispatched by hooks.after_preventing_death from DamageCmd.deal's prevented-death branch (cmds.py:106-113)
AfterPreventingDeath.issue: Rollup of guards G1 and G2 per binding rule 4. The C# body is one line -- `await OnUseWrapper(new ThrowingPlayerChoiceContext(), creature)` (FairyInABottle.cs:42-45) -- i.e. the automatic trigger runs the FULL use pipeline, the same one a manual drink runs. The sim hand-rolls a two-line substitute (`discard_potion` then `self.use(...)`) that reproduces only two of that pipeline's ten steps, and in particular never dispatches Hook.AfterPotionUsed (G1). The heal arithmetic itself is right (N1).

OnUse (protected override, FairyInABottl.rationale: See guard N1 -- the heal amount is equal on both sides despite being expressed differently.

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): the automatic trigger bypasses OnUseWrapper, so Hook.AfterPotionUsed never fires when the fairy pops
guards.issue: MECHANISM: FairyInABottle.cs:44 goes through `OnUseWrapper`, so every step of PotionModel.cs:291-342 runs -- including :338 `Hook.AfterPotionUsed`. The sim's after_preventing_death (potions.py:1245-1250) calls `combat.player.discard_potion(self)` and then `self.use(combat._ctx(), creature)` directly, and `grep -rn on_potion_used sts2_rl/` shows the ONLY dispatch site is combat.py:610, inside CombatState.use_potion -- which this path does not go through. So in the sim an automatic potion use is invisible to every AfterPotionUsed listener. LIVE on ported content: the two C# AfterPotionUsed implementers are BeltBuckle.cs:81 and ReptileTrinket.cs:22 and both are ported with working on_potion_used handlers (relics/belt_buckle.py:32-33, relics/reptile_trinket.py:23-29 -- audit/records/relic/reptile_trinket.json verdicts that hook faithful at its own site). Concretely: holding Reptile Trinket and a Fairy in a Bottle, the game grants 3 temporary Strength when the fairy saves you and the sim grants none; holding Belt Buckle, the game re-applies 2 Dexterity the moment the fairy leaves the belt and the sim does not. Both relics are in the transcribed grab bag and the fairy is a pooled Rare. This is a DIFFERENT defect from the shared W entry: W is about BeforePotionUsed and CheckForEmptyHand being absent from the pipeline; this is about this unit skipping the pipeline altogether. Also skipped: the belt/run history entries and CheckForEmptyHand.

guards.what: G2 (dormant): `discard_potion` is the DiscardPotionInternal verb; OnUseWrapper's first step is RemoveBeforeUse, a different one
guards.issue: PotionModel has two removal verbs with different meanings: Discard() -> `Owner.DiscardPotionInternal(this)` (PotionModel.cs:221-225), used by PotionCmd.Discard which then fires `Hook.AfterPotionDiscarded` (PotionCmd.cs:55-60), and RemoveBeforeUse() -> `Owner.RemoveUsedPotionInternal(this)` (PotionModel.cs:230-234), which fires nothing. The fairy takes the SECOND route (via OnUseWrapper), so its disappearance is a USE, not a discard, and AfterPotionDiscarded listeners must not fire. potions.py:1249 calls `combat.player.discard_potion`, whose name says discard and whose inline comment says 'RemoveBeforeUse'. DORMANT because the sim's discard_potion (player.py:123-127) does not dispatch any discard hook either -- it only nulls the slot and detaches the listener -- so today the two verbs are indistinguishable in the sim and nothing observable follows. What would make it live: wiring Hook.AfterPotionDiscarded (Belt Buckle's missing AfterPotionDiscarded half is already a gap in audit/records/relic/belt_buckle.json) onto the sim's discard_potion, at which point the fairy would wrongly trigger it. Recorded so that fix does not silently create a defect.

guards.what: N1: the heal -- C# heals BY `max(MaxHp*0.3, 1)` from 0 HP; the sim heals UP TO `max(max_hp*30//100, 1)` from 1 HP
guards.rationale: SETTLED BY ARITHMETIC, because the two expressions look different and the sim's docstring asserts they agree (PROMPT.md bug class 24 says verdict the code, not the comment). C#: the prevented death leaves CurrentHp at 0 (CreatureCmd.cs:565 -- the game does not restore HP itself), then CreatureCmd.Heal -> HealInternal -> SetCurrentHpInternal does `CurrentHp = (int)Math.Min(0 + MaxHp*0.3m, MaxHp)` (Creature.cs:477-491), and the decimal->int cast truncates, so the final HP is trunc(0.3*MaxHp) with a floor of 1. Sim: DamageCmd.deal floors the prevented death at `target.hp = 1` (cmds.py:112) and THEN calls after_preventing_death, so potions.py:1255-1256 computes `heal_to = max(max_hp*30//100, 1)` and heals by `heal_to - creature.hp` = heal_to - 1, landing on heal_to. `max_hp*30//100` is floor(0.3*max_hp) and equals trunc for non-negative values, so both land on the same HP. Worked: max_hp 80 -> 24 on both sides; max_hp 83 -> C# trunc(24.9) = 24, sim 2490//100 = 24. The 1-HP floor also agrees (`Math.Max(..., 1m)` vs `max(..., 1)`). The intermediate state does differ -- the sim is at 1 HP where C# is at 0 while the preventer runs -- and that is audit/records/seam/damage_pipeline.json guard G4's mechanism, not this record's.

guards.what: N2: the fairy stops listening the moment it leaves the belt, so it cannot prevent two deaths
guards.rationale: The re-entrancy question a death-prevention listener always raises. C#: RemoveBeforeUse sets HasBeenRemovedFromState (PotionModel.cs:230-234), and CombatState.Contains drops any potion with that flag from the listener walk (audit/records/seam/hook_dispatch.json step 12). Sim: player.discard_potion nulls the slot and calls detach_potion, which unregisters it from the HookSystem (player.py:123-136) -- and the sim's own docstring names that as 'what stops a used Fairy in a Bottle from preventing death again'. Different machinery, same observable. Note the sim's removal is EAGER where C#'s is a lazy per-item filter, which is hook_dispatch gap G7's mechanism and dormant there.

guards.what: N3: `ShouldDie` is consulted while the potion merely SITS in the belt -- the potion is a hook listener without being used
guards.rationale: This is the whole reason a potion is in the listener walk at all, and both sides do it. C#: CombatState.IterateHookListeners walks each player's PotionSlots (audit/records/seam/hook_dispatch.json step 6). Sim: combat.py:164-166 registers every held potion at combat setup and player.add_potion registers one procured mid-combat (player.py:119-120). EXECUTED census: `py audit/tools/potion_probes.py sweep-hooks` finds exactly one potion overriding an AbstractModel hook on the C# side (fairy_in_a_bottle: ShouldDie, AfterPreventingDeath) and exactly one on the sim side, the same unit -- agreeing with hook_dispatch step 15's independent probe. So no other potion in this tier has belt-resident behaviour to check. The POSITION of potions in the listener order is hook_dispatch gap G2 and is not re-verdicted here.

guards.what: W: the shared PotionModel.OnUseWrapper pipeline every potion resolves through (audit/content/potion/shared-mechanisms.md)
guards.issue: MECHANISM, shared by all 51 units and recorded once per record because PotionModel is one of harness.py's MODEL_ROOT_CLASSES, so no unit record enumerates it -- and unlike CardModel/PowerModel/RelicModel it is NOT covered by any seam record either, which is the coverage hole audit/content/potion/shared-mechanisms.md exists to name. src/Core/Models/PotionModel.cs:291-342 in order: :293 RemoveBeforeUse (sim combat.py:603-606 nulls the slot and detaches the listener before the effect -- faithful); :297 Hook.BeforePotionUsed; :327 OnUse (this record's own hooks); :336 CombatManager.History.PotionUsed (no sim entry -- PotionUsedEntry.cs:9-38 adds only a Description string and an executed grep of src/ finds no game reader, so presentation only); :338 Hook.AfterPotionUsed (sim hooks.py:566-571 on_potion_used, dispatched at combat.py:610 -- faithful); :340 CheckForEmptyHand. TWO of those are LIVE gaps, and both are already owned by another record, so this entry MATCHES their verdicts per binding rule 3 rather than re-deriving them. (1) BeforePotionUsed has no sim dispatcher at all -- hooks.py declares only on_potion_used, whose own docstring says it mirrors AfterPotionUsed -- and its single C# implementer SurroundedPower.cs:82 is ported at powers.py:2523, so throwing a potion at the far Kaiser Crab arm does not turn the player to face it: audit/records/power/surrounded.json, gap, live. (2) CombatManager.cs:887-893 CheckForEmptyHand has exactly two callers, CardModel.cs:1992 and PotionModel.cs:340, and the sim's only on_hand_emptied call site is player.py:197 -- the end-of-turn flush CombatManager.cs:880-883 explicitly excludes: audit/records/relic/unceasing_top.json G1, gap, LIVE, executed with a potion witness. Reachable from EVERY potion, not only the hand-emptying ones, because C# tests the hand AFTER the use. Rollup `gap` per binding rule 4.

guards.what: W4: PotionModel.cs:324-331 brackets OnUse in BeginCardOrPotionEffect/EndCardOrPotionEffect and the sim has no re-entrancy depth counter
guards.issue: CombatManager.cs:889's `!IsExecutingCardOrPotionEffect(player)` is what stops a nested effect from triggering the empty-hand check early, and PotionModel.cs:324-331 is what puts a potion inside that bracket. The sim has no counterpart anywhere. DORMANT for the same reason audit/records/relic/unceasing_top.json G2 is dormant -- the ported cards that auto-play another card mid-resolution (cards/cascade.py:58, cards/colorless_skills.py:117) do not touch the draw pile between the inner and outer ends -- but recorded separately because the OUTER frame here is a potion, so a fix that brackets only card plays would leave this half open. What would make it live: any ported potion or card that empties the hand and then moves the draw pile from inside a nested auto-play.
